title: The Declassified NSA Report on a Star That Vanished Instantly
hook: A star in a distant galaxy didn't explode, collapse, or fade—it just stopped existing in a single frame of telescope data.
why_this_can_go_viral: Combines classified government files with an impossible cosmic event—two viral hooks in one.

title: The Rogue Planet That Radiates Pure Microwave Energy
hook: A planetless star system emits a beam that could cook electronics from across the solar system.
why_this_can_go_viral: Immediate threat to modern electronics creates a visceral 'what if' fear.

title: The Black Hole That Spews Out Time-Reversed Light
hook: Light coming from this black hole appears to move backward, suggesting causality itself is breaking down at the event horizon.
why_this_can_go_viral: Time reversal is an instantly mind-bending concept that sparks endless discussion.

title: The Galaxy That Emits a Signal Only Plants on Earth Can Detect
hook: Chlorophyll fluorescence on Earth matches a frequency coming from a galaxy 200 million light-years away.
why_this_can_go_viral: Links cosmic mystery to biology—viewers feel personally connected to the signal.

title: The Asteroid That Had a Nuclear Power Source Inside
hook: When NASA scanned this asteroid's interior, they found a steady heat signature that could only come from fission.
why_this_can_go_viral: The idea of a 'nuclear bomb from space' taps into deep existential fear.

title: The Classified UK File on a Meteor That Crashed Into a Military Base
hook: A meteor struck a British army base in 1991—the file says 'object retrieved' but no meteorite was ever shown to scientists.
why_this_can_go_viral: Military cover-up plus a mysterious retrieved object is an evergreen conspiracy magnet.

title: The Dark Matter Cloud That Caused a Global Seismic Event
hook: In 2018, the entire Earth rang like a bell for 20 minutes—scientists now believe a dark matter wave passed through the planet.
why_this_can_go_viral: Links an invisible, terrifying force to a real global event—feels like a sci-fi movie premise.

title: The Comet That Left a Trail of Pure Helium-3
hook: Helium-3 is the fuel of the future—and this comet dropped enough to power Earth for a century.
why_this_can_go_viral: Combines 'free energy' hope with the unsettling question of who left it.

title: The Extinction Event That Was a Superflare from a Dead Star
hook: A white dwarf—a star that should be dead—unleashed a flare that could strip an atmosphere from 50 light-years away.
why_this_can_go_viral: The concept of a 'dead' star still being lethal is deeply unsettling and counterintuitive.

title: The Rogue Planet That Reflects No Light at All
hook: A planet-sized object absorbs 99.9% of all light that hits it—and it's drifting toward the inner solar system.
why_this_can_go_viral: A 'perfectly black' planet is visually striking and creates a 'what if it hits us' dread.

title: The Secret Space Force Recording of an Object That Changed Course
hook: A classified US Space Force audio log captures an object making a 90-degree turn at Mach 30—no known physics allows that.
why_this_can_go_viral: Government-adjacent proof of impossible technology is the holy grail of UFO content.

title: The Stellar Flare That Synchronized with Earth's Power Grid
hook: A solar flare in 1967 pulsed at exactly the same frequency as the US power grid—causing a nationwide blackout on purpose.
why_this_can_go_viral: Blends a real historical event with the implication of a targeted cosmic attack.

title: The Dark Matter Particle That Causes Alzheimer's
hook: A study from CERN suggests a rare dark matter particle interacts with the human brain—and may be linked to rising neurological disease rates.
why_this_can_go_viral: Personal health threat from a cosmic source creates a powerful 'this affects me' hook.

title: The Signal That Was a Blueprint for a Dyson Sphere
hook: A repeating signal from a star 400 light-years away contained nanosecond-precision instructions for building a shell around a sun.
why_this_can_go_viral: Combines a classic sci-fi concept (Dyson sphere) with a 'real signal' narrative.

title: The Comet That Carried a Cannibalistic Genetic Code
hook: DNA found on a comet included a gene that forces any cell to consume its neighbors—a literal 'kill switch' from space.
why_this_can_go_viral: Biological horror from space is deeply primal and shareable.

title: The Stellar Flare That Incinerated a Planet from the Inside Out
hook: A flare's energy didn't heat the surface—it bypassed the atmosphere and ignited the planet's core, turning it into a bomb.
why_this_can_go_viral: The idea of a fire 'from the inside out' is visually and conceptually horrifying.

title: The Rogue Planet That Creates Gravity Lenses Smaller Than a Coin
hook: This planet bends light so intensely that it creates microscopic lensing effects—visible only as flickers in telescope data.
why_this_can_go_viral: A 'tiny gravity lens' is a strange, almost magical concept that invites curiosity.

title: The Classified Russian Photo of a Diamond Sphere in Orbit
hook: A declassified Soviet military photo shows a perfect geometric sphere with diamond-like reflectance orbiting Earth—no nation claimed it.
why_this_can_go_viral: Visual evidence of an unexplained object in orbit is a guaranteed viral hit.

title: The Signal That Was a Literal 'Hello World' in Binary
hook: A burst from a dead star contained the exact binary sequence for 'Hello World'—the first program every coder learns.
why_this_can_go_viral: Relatable to programmers and general audience—a 'hello' from the void is chilling and exciting.

title: The Extinction Event That Was a Precision Asteroid Swarm—Guided
hook: A series of asteroids hit Earth in perfect geometric pattern over 24 hours—as if guided by a targeting system.
why_this_can_go_viral: The idea of a 'guided' extinction event feels like the plot of a horror movie—deeply shareable.
